root_idea.summary: The root centers on slipping or moving away from a position, course, or stable state.
root_idea.development: From physical displacement and the ease of sliding, the root extends to deviation and error, while reduplicated forms express repeated agitation or violent motion; clear, sweet water is described as slipping easily from the tongue.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested Form I verb, normalized to the classical citation form زَلَّ.
Distinct Quran-attested Form IV causative verb.
Distinct Quran-attested Form X verb expressing attempted or induced slipping.

senses.definition: To slip, move aside, or deviate; hence, to lapse or err.
senses.usage_conditions: Used intransitively for physical slipping or movement from a place, and figuratively for deviation or a lapse in speech, judgment, action, religion, or the right course.

senses.definition: To cause someone to slip or fall away, including into error.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive causative use, applicable to physical slipping or displacement and to inducing a wrong action or deviation; in the Quranic occurrence, persons are caused to slip from a place.

senses.definition: To seek to make someone slip or fall into error; to lead someone into a lapse.
senses.usage_conditions: A transitive, intentional or attempted induction into slipping, including seeking out or exploiting another person's lapse; the Quranic usage describes being drawn into error until one slips.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take or receive something given, especially food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive counterpart inferred in legal usage from أَزَلَّ إِلَيْهِ, “he gave to him.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a benefit to pass or be transferred from a benefactor to another person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a benefit or favor moving from its giver to its recipient.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pass along quickly or run; to move lightly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of rapid or light movement, including the movement of camels between places.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a person's life to pass or glide away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of passing or moving away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For money to pour forth, or to become deficient in weight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of dirhams or other pieces of money.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Leanness in the hips, haunches, buttocks, or thighs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A physical description of insufficient flesh.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be made or rendered thin or slender.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical usage equated with دُقِّقَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To send or put someone forward to a people or party.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use distinct from causing someone to slip.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone turn away from an opinion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively of causing a person to abandon a view.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give or bestow a benefit, gift, food, or part of what is due.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a recipient and, where specified, with food or another apportioned thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put someone or something into motion, agitation, commotion, or violent convulsion; to unsettle or alarm.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of violent movement, driving camels forcefully, the agitation of a people, and the casting of fear into them. This reduplicated derived form is Quran-attested in the supplied lexical evidence but is not a supplied QAC form group.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause liquid to pass into the throat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression used of putting water into the throat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become in a state of motion, agitation, commotion, or violent convulsion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used intransitively of the earth or other things; of the soul, it can describe its heaving in the chest at death.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slippery place or surface on which the foot slips.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a standing-place, smooth rock, slope, or slide.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slip, lapse, fault, wrong action, mistake, or error; sometimes a sin or crime.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for an unintended or blameworthy lapse, especially in speech, conduct, or judgment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A benefit, good action, gift, or favor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun distinct from زَلَّةٌ meaning a fault.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A feast or repast prepared for guests; also a marriage feast or food carried from another's table.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Some of these uses are dialectal or colloquial.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A straitened state of the breath.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical analysis is reported with uncertainty over the underlying word in the source explanation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stone or smooth stone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is reported as زِلَلٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A deficiency, especially a deficiency in weight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a shortfall in a measure or balance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small white animal said to cool or chill water when placed in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical item describing the animal itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of water: cool or cold, sweet, clear, limpid, and easy or quick to swallow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of water and its pleasant, unobstructed passage into the throat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Clear or limpid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective may be applied more generally than to water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sweet food called فَالُوذ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized food term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A carpet or a type of woollen floor covering.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A loanword and a term for a kind of woven furnishing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Household goods, utensils, or the furniture and equipment of a house or tent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use distinct from the reduplicated movement vocabulary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Light or agile, especially a light, agile boy or young man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet for physical quickness or agility.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A skilful player on the drum.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized occupational or skill description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Agitation, convulsion, or violent motion, especially an earthquake.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for violent earthly shaking; the supplied evidence also uses it in Quranic expressions, although no corresponding QAC form group was supplied.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lightness or activity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for agility or active movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Light or active in spirit and body; acute, quick, clever, or ingenious in intellect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing physical and mental liveliness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Conflict or fighting accompanied by an evil or troubled condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression تَرَكْتُ القَوْمَ فِى زُلْزُولٍ وَعُلْعُولٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Difficulties, terrors, or causes of fear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural form with an irregular or unreported singular in this usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Deficient in weight, especially said of a coin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of dirhams and dinars; plural forms are also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quick or swift.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general adjective of rapid movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having little flesh in the buttocks, hips, or thighs; lean-rumped.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person or animal, including the specifically described wolf; the feminine form is used of a woman with this physical trait.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bow from which the arrow slips because of the rapidity of its discharge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of a bow and the arrow's rapid release.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An exclamation uttered in alarm or distress.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used on occasions of violent agitation or terror; its etymological analysis is disputed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause of slipping.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proposed primary sense of this variant form; the source directs the reader to the related form مَزِلَّةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slippery place, such as a smooth rock or similar surface.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form مَزِلَّةٌ is reported as the more chaste variant; it is also used metaphorically of a hazardous path.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who bestows many benefits or gifts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participial noun for a benefactor.

cautions: Lane and Maqayis evidence is matched to the canonical geminate root زلل through the packet's contracted-root mapping; reduplicated زلزل forms are retained as lexical evidence but are not additional QAC form groups.
A historical Lane Quran citation in the Form I discussion is not converted into a modern surah:ayah location; the displayed Quran examples use only independently supplied QAC locations.
The Form I QAC lemma زَلَلْ and the supplied inflected Form IV and Form X candidates have been normalized to the classical citation forms زَلَّ, أَزَلَّ, and اِسْتَزَلَّ.
